arxiv-1909-11799.title: Manifold Oblique Random Forests: Towards Closing the Gap on Convolutional Deep Networks
arxiv-1909-11799.creator: Adam Li ∗,1,3, Ronan Perry ∗,1, Chester Huynh ∗,1,3, Tyler M. Tomita 1, Ronak Mehta 2, Jesús Arroyo 2, Jesse Patsolic 2, Benjamin Falk 2, Sridevi V. Sarma 1,3, Joshua T. Vogelstein 1,2,3
arxiv-1909-11799.description: Abstract Decision forests, in particular random forests and gradient boosting trees have demonstrated state-of-the-art accuracy compared to other methods in many supervised learning scenarios. Forests dominate other methods in tabular data, that is, when the feature space is unstructured, so that the signal is invariant to a permutation of the feature indices.

arxiv-2005-11889.title: EARLY MASS VARYING NEUTRINO DARK ENERGY: NUGGET FORMATION AND HUBBLE ANOMALY Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2005-11889.creator: Antareep Gogoi, Ravi Kumar Sharma, Prolay Chanda, Subinoy Das
arxiv-2005-11889.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Antareep Gogoi, Ravi Kumar Sharma, Prolay Chanda, Subinoy Das. We present a novel scenario, in which light ( ∼ \sim few eV) dark fermions (sterile neutrinos) interact with a scalar field like in mass varying neutrino dark energy theories. As the eV \rm{eV} sterile states naturally become non-relativistic before the Matter Radiation Equality (MRE), we show that the neutrino-scalar fluid develops strong perturbative instability followed by the formation of neutrino-nuggets and the early dark energy behaviour disappears around MRE.

arxiv-2304-12460.title: Functional Causal Inference with Time-to-Event Data
arxiv-2304-12460.creator: Xiyuan Gao 1, Jiayi Wang 2,∗, Guanyu Hu 3, Jianguo Sun 4 1 xgao@mail.missouri.edu 2,∗ jiayi.wang2@utdallas.edu 3 guanyu.hu@missouri.edu 4 sunj@missouri.edu 1,3,4 Department of Statistics, University of Missouri-Columbia 2,∗ Department of Mathematical Sciences, University of Texas at Dallas
arxiv-2304-12460.description: Abstract Functional data is a powerful tool for capturing and analyzing complex patterns and relationships in a variety of fields, allowing for more precise modeling, visualization, and decision-making. For example, in healthcare, functional data such as medical images can help doctors make more accurate diagnoses and develop more effective treatment plans.

arxiv-2305-05748.title: Multilevel Sentence Embeddings for Personality Prediction
arxiv-2305-05748.creator: Paolo Tirotta ∗1, Akira Yuasa ∗1, Masashi Morita ∗1
arxiv-2305-05748.description: Abstract Representing text into a multidimensional space can be done with sentence embedding models such as Sentence-BERT (SBERT). However, training these models when the data has a complex multilevel structure requires individually trained class-specific models, which increases time and computing costs. We propose a two step approach which enables us to map sentences according to their hierarchical memberships and polarity.

arxiv-2308-14066.title: Bi-Modality Medical Image Synthesis Using Semi-Supervised Sequential Generative Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2308-14066.creator: Xin Yang, Yi Lin*, Zhiwei Wang, Xin Li, Kwang-Ting Cheng
arxiv-2308-14066.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a bi-modality medical image synthesis approach based on sequential generative adversarial network (GAN) and semi-supervised learning. Our approach consists of two generative modules that synthesize images of the two modalities in a sequential order. A method for measuring the synthesis complexity is proposed to automatically determine the synthesis order in our sequential GAN.

arxiv-2406-16388.title: PenSLR: Persian end-to-end Sign Language Recognition Using Ensembling
arxiv-2406-16388.creator: Amirparsa Salmankhah, Amirreza Rajabi, Negin Kheirmand, Ali Fadaeimanesh, Amirreza Tarabkhah, Amirreza Kazemzadeh, Hamed Farbeh
arxiv-2406-16388.description: Abstract . Sign Language Recognition (SLR) is a fast-growing field that aims to fill the communication gaps between the hearing-impaired and people without hearing loss. Existing solutions for Persian Sign Language (PSL) are limited to word-level interpretations, underscoring the need for more advanced and comprehensive solutions.

arxiv-2510-06103.title: Helicity correlation of dihadron in current and target fragmentation regions of unpolarized SIDIS
arxiv-2510-06103.creator: Xue-Qi Xi, Kai-Bao Chen, Xuan-Bo Tong, Shu-Yi Wei, Jing Wu
arxiv-2510-06103.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xue-Qi Xi, Kai-Bao Chen, Xuan-Bo Tong, Shu-Yi Wei, Jing Wu. We study the helicity correlation of two Λ \Lambda hyperons produced in unpolarized semi-inclusive deep inelastic scatterings (SIDIS), with one hyperon detected in the current fragmentation region and the other in the target fragmentation region. This observable provides direct access to the spin-dependent fragmentation function G 1 ​ L ​ q G_{1Lq} and the spin-dependent fracture function l 1 ​ q L l_{1q}^{L} even in unpolarized lepton nucleon collisions.

arxiv-2511-07879.title: Planned Event Forecasting using Future Mentions and Related Entity Extraction in News Articles
arxiv-2511-07879.creator: Neelesh K Shukla, Pranay Sanghvi
arxiv-2511-07879.description: Abstract In democracies like India, people are free to express their views and demands. Sometimes which causes the situation of civil unrest like protest, rallies, marches etc. These events may be disruptive in nature and most of the times held without taking prior permission from competent authority. Forecasting these events will help administrative officials to take necessary action.

pmc-11388208.title: Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy: a narrative review of systems
pmc-11388208.creator: Sebastian Fernandez-Bussy, Nikitha C Chandra, Anoop Koratala, Alejandra Yu Lee-Mateus, Alanna Barrios-Ruiz, Ana Garza-Salas, Tapendra Koirala, Rodrigo Funes-Ferrada, Prasanth Balasubramanian, Neal M Patel, Ryan Chadha, Britney N Hazelett, Kelly S Robertson, Janani Reisenauer, David Abia-Trujillo
pmc-11388208.description: Background and ObjectiveRobotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) has emerged as an advanced technology for lung cancer diagnosis. This review explores the three approved robotic bronchoscopy systems: Ion™ Endoluminal (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA, USA), Monarch™ (Johnson & Johnson, Redwood City, CA, USA), and Galaxy System™ (Noah Medical, San Carlos, CA, USA), and their different operational systems.

pmc-11570810.title: Single-cell sequencing unveils mitophagy-related prognostic model for triple-negative breast cancer
pmc-11570810.creator: Peikai Ding, Shengbin Pei, Zheng Qu, Yazhe Yang, Qiang Liu, Xiangyi Kong, Zhongzhao Wang, Jing Wang, Yi Fang
pmc-11570810.description: BackgroundTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer lacking hormone receptors and HER2 expression, leading to limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Mitophagy, a selective autophagy process targeting damaged mitochondria, plays a complex role in cancer progression, yet its prognostic significance in TNBC is not well understood.

pmc-11676970.description: Microbial attack, particularly fungal degradation of cellulose, is a leading cause of paper damage. pmc-11710186.description: BackgroundRecent studies suggest that among cognitively unimpaired older adults, there are individuals who might present with subtle cognitive impairments suggesting the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD; Bos et al., 2018). The Visual Short‐Term Memory Binding Test (VSTMBT) identifies older adults who are accumulating AD pathology even though they are otherwise cognitively unimpaired (Parra et al., 2024).

pmc-13542040.title: Lightweight Transformer-based knowledge distillation framework for high-dimensional spatiotemporal radiomics in breast cancer risk prediction
pmc-13542040.creator: Haofan Huang, Han Zhou, Kaibin Huang, Jie Yang, Peixi Ying, Puxiang Lai, Yan Lin, Yi Gao
pmc-13542040.description: Breast cancer exhibits significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Traditional radiomics approaches usually rely on low-temporal-resolution imaging and discrete image phases, failing to capture the rapid and continuous kinetic evolution within the tumor microenvironment. Although ultrafast dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging captures precise contrast agent permeation, current methodologies lack systematic, dedicated computational frameworks to extract these high-dimensional dynamic features.
